The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the RMS Titanic.

To explain the complex concept of blockchain using an analogy: Imagine a community notebook where everyone writes down every transaction that happens in their town. Instead of keeping this notebook in one locked safe at the bank (a centralized system), every single resident has an identical copy of the notebook at home.

When a new transaction occurs, such as Alice paying Bob $10, Alice announces it to the whole town. The residents then check their own notebooks to make sure Alice actually has $10. If the majority of residents agree that the transaction is valid, they all update their individual notebooks simultaneously.

This makes the system extremely secure because:
1.  **Decentralization:** There is no single point of failure. If one person’s notebook is lost or destroyed, the rest of the town still has the correct record.
2.  **Immutability:** Once a page is filled and agreed upon by the majority, it cannot be erased or altered. If someone tries to sneak into their house and change their notebook to say they still have the $10, the other 999 residents will notice the discrepancy when they compare notes, and the change will be rejected.

This collective verification process ensures that the ledger is trustworthy without needing a central authority like a bank to oversee it.
